Implementation for the following POSIX signal APIs:

- [`int sigemptyset(sigset_t *set);`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigemptyset.html#)
- [`int sigfillset(sigset_t *set);`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigfillset.html#)
- [`int sigaddset(sigset_t *set, int signo);`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigaddset.html#)
- [`int sigdelset(sigset_t *set, int signo);`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigdelset.html#)
- [`int sigismember(const sigset_t *set, int signo);`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigismember.html#)
- [`char *strsignal(int signum);`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/strsignal.html#)

fixes #59929

Reviewing the functions provided, what's the use case for this functionality? Are there plans to extend this to provide `signal` and `raise`? How about the pthread signal functions like `pthread_kill`? Given how difficult most developers find this particular programming model, I could build a fairly strong argument for just not providing any of this functionality and having developers use other communication mechanisms instead ...

> Reviewing the functions provided, what's the use case for this functionality? Are there plans to extend this to provide `signal` and `raise`?

Currently, we have no plans to (fully) support the `POSIX_MULTI_PROCESS` subprofiling option, since Zephyr hasn't really ventured into that space yet, so probably not `signal()` and `raise()` (maybe only if there is a certain use case for it). Some parts of it are already supported (e.g. assert, exit, sleep, exit, ..)

> How about the pthread signal functions like `pthread_kill`?

Yes `pthread_kill()` and `pthread_sigmask()` are the only things I can see working in a single-process environment. 

> Given how difficult most developers find this particular programming model, I could build a fairly strong argument for just not providing any of this functionality and having developers use other communication mechanisms instead ...

It's definitely easier to use other communication mechanisms, and so this will be defaulted to N, of course. It's mainly going to be there to have something for external libraries to link with.

One particular thing to note is that we will likely never interrupt any system call. So there is a bit of wiggle room in the mechanism for "delivering" signals even.

> Currently, we have no plans to (fully) support the `POSIX_MULTI_PROCESS` subprofiling option, since Zephyr hasn't really ventured into that space yet, so probably not `signal()` and `raise()` (maybe only if there is a certain use case for it). Some parts of it are already supported (e.g. assert, exit, sleep, exit, ..)

There's a whole mess of interrelated functions in the C spec (these aren't  POSIX, after all). `assert` is defined to call `abort`, `abort` is defined to call `raise(SIGABRT)`, and that requires that `signal` be available to specify a handler. These all work fine in a single process environment; the C standard doesn't even mention the `kill` function, after all. 

Now, whether you want to follow the C spec for `assert` is a whole 'nuther story; I've never heard of anyone trapping `SIGABRT` and doing anything with the result, but I can't say it couldn't happen. And, in an embedded system, it's actually pretty plausible for the application to want to perform some specific logging and error recovery when assertions fail, so maybe this whole thing might actually be useful to someone?

> It's definitely easier to use other communication mechanisms, and so this will be defaulted to N, of course. It's mainly going to be there to have something for external libraries to link with.

Yeah, makes sense. One suspects those will call `signal` a bunch of times to ignore fun POSIX things like SIGTSTP, and maybe mess with sigmasks just for fun.

> One particular thing to note is that we will likely never interrupt any system call. So there is a bit of wiggle room in the mechanism for "delivering" signals even.

Given that you aren't even defining an OS-delivered signals, or the `kill` function, I don't think there's any issue here. Consider whether you want to support the C standard interpretation of signal handling and how much of the fancier POSIX stuff you want to bolt on as well.

@keith-packard - if we're going to tackle the ISO C variants of signal, etc, it will likely be later. Potentially some interesting implications though, for sure.

issue_context.title: posix: implement `sigaddset()`
issue_context.body:
There are currently 20 missing POSIX functions with trivial implementations, `sigaddset()` is one of them.

> sigaddset - add a signal to a signal set
> 
> The sigaddset() function adds the individual signal specified by the signo to the signal set pointed to by set.
> 
> Applications shall call either [sigemptyset()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigemptyset.html) or [sigfillset()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigfillset.html) at least once for each object of type sigset_t prior to any other use of that object. If such an object is not initialized in this way, but is nonetheless supplied as an argument to any of [pthread_sigmask()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/pthread_sigmask.html), [sigaction()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigaction.html), sigaddset(), [sigdelset()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigdelset.html), [sigismember()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigismember.html), [sigpending()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigpending.html), [sigprocmask()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigprocmask.html), [sigsuspend()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigsuspend.html), [sigtimedwait()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigtimedwait.html), [sigwait()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigwait.html), or [sigwaitinfo()](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigwaitinfo.html), the results are undefined.

See https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/sigaddset.html

See RFC #51211 for more info.
